correctness.rationale: Universal argument: m<=3 cannot contain a cycle; distinct 4-cycles overlap in at most 2 edges, ruling out m=5. Edge-girth four implies triangle-free, so Mantel gives n>=ceil(2 sqrt(m)). For n least admissible and m>=7, a=floor(n/2),b=ceil(n/2),d=ab-m satisfies a,b>=3 and 0<=d<=a-1. K_(a,b) minus a d-edge matching has n vertices and m edges. Each surviving edge has nonempty opposite-neighbor candidate sets; absence of a 4-cycle would force a=b=3 and three distinct matching deletions, contradicting d<=2. Same-part common neighbors prove connectedness. C4 and K_(2,3) handle m=4,6. Reproducible exhaustive enumeration 33,861 graphs on at most 6 vertices and checks of 2,996 explicit witnesses match, without treating finite checking as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest relevant general coverage bound is Mantel: no triangle-free graph with m edges can use fewer than ceil(2 sqrt(m)) vertices. This gives a lower bound only. The present construction proves that this bound is attainable subject to the strictly stronger every-edge-on-four-cycle constraint at every admissible size. The paper’s maximum-diameter result optimizes a different invariant and does not supply the missing order-minimal construction.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison to Marey–Hilaire–Laclau full text, especially Theorem 6.1 and Sections 7–8, demonstrates a minimum-order question not solved by their existence and maximum-diameter results; the classical Mantel bound lacks the needed square-coverage construction. Nine actual published-record queries and seven external literature queries across aliases found no covering statement. Unindexed equivalent work remains possible.

value.rationale: An exact minimum vertex budget for every constant-four edge-girth realization is a natural infinite-family subproblem of the expressly proposed vertex-number realization problem (Marey et al., Section 8). The theorem shows zero vertex overhead relative to Mantel despite every edge requiring membership in a quadrilateral, and supplies a uniform extremal construction. The result cannot be obtained as a mere renaming or direct substitution into the motivating paper’s existence/diameter theorems. It does not claim a broader theorem for all edge-girth constants.
